g.text: Only one table is a source of truth. Everything else is bookkeeping or a projection.
And the strongest guarantee in the system applies to an append-only log, while the weakest applies to what users actually read.
sequence is monotonic WITHIN a partition, not
globally - a global sequence would need cross-
partition coordination on every event, the exact
bottleneck being eliminated. Per-partition is FREE
(the Raft leader assigns it) and SUFFICIENT, because
the only ordering that must be total is one
ACCOUNT's - and an account never moves partitions.
occurred_at is stamped ONCE at command time and
stored IN the row, so replay uses the recorded
No UPDATE or DELETE grant on this table, ever.
Compensation appends a new row with compensates_leg
set. Enforcing append-only in PERMISSIONS rather
than by convention is how you keep it true at 3am.
Why these MUST be in the replicated log rather than
local bookkeeping: applied_legs is what makes a leg
idempotent. If it lived in the leader's memory, then
on failover the NEW leader would have no record and
would happily apply a retried leg a second time.
cancelled_legs is the out-of-order tombstone - a
marker for an operation that has not arrived yet.
NOT a source of truth about money
This records the coordinator's INTENT AND BELIEF.
The events log records what HAPPENED. They can
disagree - that is the whole point of UNCERTAIN.
A timeout is resolved by reading applied_legs on
the partition, never by trusting phase_status. If
it were authoritative, a timeout would have to be
read as success or failure - and both mint money.
A CACHE, not a record. Losing
The events table IS the double-entry ledger
THEN -amount_minor ELSE amount_minor END) AS net
HAVING net <> 0; -- MUST return zero rows
A Debited row and a Credited row are the two halves of one entry - which is why
there is no separate ledger table to disagree with it.
The qualification matters: during TC/C's window an in-flight transaction legitimately
sums non-zero. So the check runs against TERMINAL transactions at a COMMITTED
SEQUENCE POSITION, never as a live scan. Under that qualification, a single non-zero
row is created or destroyed money.
The honest gap: nothing in this design runs it on a schedule with an alert. Writing
down an invariant without automating its check is how it quietly stops being true.
Where the guarantees go - and note the inversion
events LINEARIZABLE within a partition (Raft quorum) <- the strongest guarantee, on an append-only log
applied_legs / cancelled_legs LINEARIZABLE, same log - committed atomically with the event they describe
cross-partition (a transfer) EVENTUAL, bounded by the deadline - TC/C's deliberate concession
phase_status / idempotency strong, read-your-writes - a stale read double-compensates or mints
balances / history EVENTUAL, ms to seconds - staleness exposed via as_of_sequence
snapshots no guarantee needed - derivable from the log
Inverted from most designs: expensive guarantees are bought only on the ~200k events/sec write path, never on the far larger
read volume. That is what makes the throughput numbers work.
